title: CLO Skills Workshop - Snap Button Production
description: Using CLO, you can create exquisite snap fasteners! Follow the CLO expert to learn the quick method of making snap fasteners!
transcript:
Hello everyone, today I will show you how to make a four-core buckle.  
First of all, the four-core buckle is divided into a combined state and an open state.  
Here we will first explain the four-core buckle in a combined state.  
Let's take the front door handle as an example.  
You can see that the corresponding panel also has a four-core buckle.  
First of all, we use the hook and loop tool to hook the circle of the buckle into the inner line or shape.  
Then use the sewing tool to sew them together.  
Open the simulation.  
In this way, we can simulate a four-core buckle in a combined state.  
Next, we see the surface of the door handle.  
If our four-core buckle does not have a face button, we need to hide the trace of the sewing line.  
Here we can use the editor sewing line tool to select the sewing line just added and change its hairline strength to 0.  
In this way, we have a four-core buckle without a face button.  
If we have a face button, we need to use the add button tool to add a button to the door handle.  
On the right side of the door handle, we select the added button to modify its shape, size, and material.  
Its color, surface light intensity, reflection intensity, etc. can be modified.  
Next, let's rotate the view.  
You can see that there is still a gap between the button and the fabric of the clothing.  
Here we use the select button.  
In this way, we can use the select move button tool.  
Select this button in front of us.  
Then, on the right side of the door handle, change the length of the line to a negative value.  
Let our button stick to our fabric.  
At the same time, we also need to close the gap between the button and the fabric of the door handle on the door handle.  
To avoid a conflict between the button and the fabric when we simulate.  
This is our door handle.  
This is how we make a four-core buckle in the combined state.  
Next, let's see how the four-core buckle works.  
The face button is still the same method.  
If there is no face button, we can skip this step.  
Next, let's add the purple button and the mother button.  
You can see that the purple button should be added on the reverse side of the door handle.  
The mother button is on the collar.  
We find the body window.  
In the button column, click on add two default buttons.  
Then, name them separately as the purple button and the mother button.  
Next, we choose the purple button.  
Use the add button tool to add it to our door handle.  
The position of our face button is the same.  
Next, we switch the tool to the select move button tool.  
Select the two buttons that we just added.  
Then, click on the right button to find the flip button.  
Flip them to the reverse side of our fabric.  
Then, in the body window, we select the current purple button.  
To modify its shape, size, and material.  
In the same way, let's make the mother button.  
Next, we use the top button to adjust its height.  
Finally, let's use the button tool to adjust the length of the button.  
Let them stick to the surface of our fabric.  
Turn off the conflict of the button.  
To prevent a conflict of the button in the later simulation.  
Continue to increase the perspective of the button.  
This is the production method of our four-core buckle.

chunks.content: ## Four-Core Buckle Production Overview This section explains the process of creating a four-core buckle in CLO, focusing on its two states: combined and open. It covers the use of hook and loop tools, sewing tools, button addition, and adjustment techniques to simulate realistic buckle behavior on garment panels. --- ## Creating a Four-Core Buckle in Combined State The four-core buckle has two main states: combined and open. This section details the steps to produce the buckle in the combined state using a front door handle example. 1. **Attaching the Buckle:** - Use the hook and loop tool to hook the circle of the buckle into the inner line or shape on the garment panel. - Use the sewing tool to sew these parts together. 2. **Simulating the Combined State:** - Open the simulation to visualize the four-core buckle in the combined state. 3. **Managing Sewing Lines:** - If the buckle does not include a face button, hide the sewing line trace. - Use the editor sewing line tool to select the added sewing line and set its hairline strength to 0, making the line invisible. 4. **Adding a Face Button (Optional):** - If the buckle requires a face button, use the add button tool to place a button on the door handle. - Modify the button’s properties such as shape, size, material, color, surface light intensity, and reflection intensity on the right panel. 5. **Adjusting Button Position:** - Rotate the view to inspect the button's placement. - If there is a gap between the button and the fabric, use the select move button tool. - Select the button and adjust the line length to a negative value to make the button stick to the fabric tightly. - Close any remaining gaps to avoid conflicts during simulation. This process ensures the buckle appears correctly attached and realistic in the combined state. --- ## Four-Core Buckle Function and Button Configuration This section covers how the four-core buckle functions with or without a face button, and how to add and configure complementary buttons such as the purple button and mother button. 1. **Face Button Considerations:** - If the buckle lacks a face button, you can skip related steps. 2. **Adding Purple and Mother Buttons:** - The purple button is added to the reverse side of the door handle. - The mother button is placed on the collar. - Access the body window, then in the button column, click to add two default buttons and rename them as “purple button” and “mother button.” 3. **Positioning and Flipping Buttons:** - Use the add button tool to place the purple button on the door handle. - Use the select move button tool to select both buttons. - Use the flip button option to flip them to the reverse side of the fabric. 4. **Modifying Button Properties:** - Select each button in the body window to adjust shape, size, and material. 5.
